map.Where it all begins — five chapters, six: Where it all begins. Five chapters, six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Field day: cancelled. Crew: soaked. My n: Field day: off. Crew: wet. My notebook: still dry. Good.
map.I'm Theo. I said it would rain. I had ch: I'm Theo. I said it would rain. I had charts.
map.Axiom City — a coastal city built on mat: Axiom City is a city by the sea. A genius named Ada Vex built it with math. She is gone. Meet Maya, Theo, Zara, and Dev. You're the fifth.
map.That dome! The door's propped open — GO: That dome! The door is open. GO GO GO!
map.Vexhall Observatory? Sealed since foreve: Vexhall's star tower? Shut for ages. Five stars for spooky.
map.I'm Maya — that's Theo, Zara, and Dev. W: I'm Maya. That's Theo, Zara, and Dev. We come in peace. And puddles.
I know. Book keepers know it all. Ms. Ortiz. Welcome to Vexhall.
map.Vexhall Observatory — built by Ada Vex,: Vexhall's star tower. Ada Vex built it. She was a math builder. She planned half of Axiom City. Then she was gone.
map.Inside: brass, dust, and ten thousand bo: Inside: brass, dust, and ten thousand books.
map.Ada Vex's last journal. Sealed sixty yea: Ada Vex's last journal. Shut for sixty years. The clasp only opens for the right fraction.
map.Three engravings — and one instruction:: Three carvings. One order: "FEED ME THE ONE BELOW ONE-HALF."
map.Use a benchmark — test each fraction aga: Use a benchmark. Test each fraction against 1/2. Is the top under half the bottom? Or over?
map.Uh… did the lamps just blink three times: Uh… did the lamps just blink? Three times. Then nine. Then twenty-seven?
map.A benchmark is a friendly reference numb: A benchmark is a nice round number, like 1/2. Test other numbers on it.
map.Reader — you're the fifth crew member no: Reader, you're the fifth crew member now. Feed the clasp the right fraction.
map.The clasp offers 3/8, 5/9, 7/12 and dema: The clasp shows 3/8, 5/9, 7/12. It wants the one below one-half. Then it checks your thinking. Tap one answer in each row.
map.Conceptual: compare each fraction to the: Conceptual: compare each fraction to the benchmark 1/2. Is its numerator smaller than HALF its denominator? Then the fraction is less than 1/2.
map.Procedural: half of 8 is 4. Half of 9 is: Procedural: half of 8 is 4. Half of 9 is 4.5. Half of 12 is 6. Compare each numerator to that half. For Clasp B, how far is 5/9 from 1/2? How far from 1?
map.Beneath the reading room. The journal's: Under the reading room. The journal's map points DOWN.
map.A door with a combination. Ada didn't tr: A door with a code lock. I guess Ada didn't trust keys.
map.Decimal dials. Easy to wreck if you don': Decimal dials. Easy to wreck if you ignore place value.
map.Write 3.6 as 3.60 — give it a hundredths: Write 3.6 as 3.60. Give it a hundredths digit. Tenths add with tenths. Hundredths add with hundredths.
map.The door is humming. Doors should NOT hu: The door is humming. Doors should NOT hum.
map.A decimal names part of a whole by place: A decimal names part of a whole. It uses place value. 3.6 means 3 ones and 6 tenths. It equals 3.60.
map.Dial carefully, reader. This door has op: Dial with care, reader. This door has opinions.
map.Two decimal dials, one rule: \"Sum, then: Two decimal dials, one rule: "Sum, then difference." Find 3.6 + 2.85 and 12.5 − 4.75 to open the door.
map.Conceptual: decimals add and subtract li: Conceptual: add and subtract decimals like whole numbers. Each digit must sit in its place-value column. Give 3.6 a hundredths digit: 3.60.
map.Procedural: Dial 1: 3.60 + 2.85 — add hu: Procedural: Dial 1: 3.60 + 2.85. Add hundredths, then tenths, then ones. Dial 2: 12.50 − 4.75. You will need to regroup.
map.Past the brass door: a corridor of glowi: Past the brass door: a hall of glowing floor tiles.
map.It's a level select! Every path is a seq: It's a level select! Each path is a sequence. It is a list in order. It has a RULE.
map.And the ceiling counts in squares. Ada h: And the ceiling counts in squares. Ada hid math in the building.
map.2 to 6 could be +4… but 6 to 18 isn't +4: 2 to 6 could be +4. But 6 to 18 isn't +4. When adding fails, try multiplying.
map.A sequence follows a rule from term to t: A sequence follows a rule from term to term. Test your rule on EVERY pair side by side. One miss means the rule is wrong. From down below, a soft voice: "…w-wake…"
map.Reader, call the next numbers — wrong st: Reader, call the next numbers. A wrong step is a glitter trap. Probably.
map.Two paths, two rules. Light the next num: Two paths, two rules. Light the next number in each sequence. The floor tiles read 2, 6, 18, 54, __. The ceiling stars read 1, 4, 9, 16, __.
map.Conceptual: a rule can multiply, not jus: Conceptual: a rule can multiply, not just add. Your move must work between EVERY pair of neighbors.
map.Procedural: Tiles — 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 18 ÷ 6: Procedural: Tiles: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3. So use that same multiplier after 54. Stars: 1 = 1×1, 4 = 2×2, 9 = 3×3, 16 = 4×4… what is the 5th?
map.h-hello. crew detected. i am VEX — fragm: Hello. Crew found. I am VEX. I am part of the Pattern Engine. Power: low. Manners: loading.
map.It's a sealed puzzle box — built from un: It's a sealed puzzle box made of unit cubes. 4 long, 3 wide, 2 tall.
map.Builder's shortcut: count one full layer: Builder's shortcut: count one full layer of cubes. Then stack the layers.
map.Ada's journal says her key sleeps inside: Ada's notes say her key sleeps in that box. Sixty years. And tonight it blinks awake.
map.Volume is the space inside a solid, meas: Volume is the space inside a solid. We count it in cubic units. Each cube is 1 unit on each edge.
map.Reader — how many cubes fill the box? Cr: Reader, how many cubes fill the box? Crack it open.
map.The sealed box is built from unit cubes:: The sealed box is made of unit cubes: 4 long, 3 wide, 2 tall. Find its volume the builder's way: one layer, then the stack.
map.Conceptual: volume counts the unit cubes: Conceptual: volume counts the unit cubes that FILL the box. Find how many cubes make one full layer. Then find how many layers stack up.
map.Procedural: the bottom layer is 4 rows o: Procedural: the bottom layer is 4 rows of 3 cubes. Multiply. The box is 2 layers tall. Multiply again.
map.Inside the box: a brass key. Below the o: Inside the box: a brass key. Under the star tower: a door. It was waiting for the key.
map.the engine ring counts in TWO rules. ada: The ring counts with TWO rules. Ada's best one: add five… then double.
map.3, 8, 16, 21, 42, 47 — and the ring stop: 3, 8, 16, 21, 42, 47. Then the ring stops. The next numbers should glow there.
Two-rule patterns. Sneaky. I like it.
map.Key fits. The ring's waiting on you, rea: Key fits. The ring waits for you, reader.
map.Some patterns alternate two rules. Keep: Some patterns use two rules in turns. Keep the order: +5, then ×2, then +5 again…
map.Light the last two numbers on the ring,: Light the last two numbers on the ring, reader!
map.The ring alternates TWO rules — +5, then: The ring uses TWO rules in turns: +5, then ×2. It reads 3, 8, 16, 21, 42, 47, __, __. Light the next two numbers.
map.Conceptual: two rules take turns. Track: Conceptual: two rules take turns. Find which rule was used LAST. The other one goes next.
map.Procedural: 3→8 is +5. 8→16 is ×2. 16→21: Procedural: 3→8 is +5. 8→16 is ×2. 16→21 is +5 again. The step into 47 was +5. So which rule goes next? And which one after that?
map.The engine core. Three locks. Power at t: The engine core. Three locks. Power at two percent.
map.three locks: one p-pattern, one decimal,: Three locks: one pattern, one decimal, one fraction. Solve all three and I can finally WAKE.
map.Everyone takes their strength. Reader —: Everyone use your strength. Reader, you take the math.
Pattern lock: my kind of level.
map.Boss Gate: use everything from this volu: Boss Gate: use all you learned in this volume. Patterns, decimals, and the 1/2 benchmark.
map.BOSS GATE. three locks. p-power at one p: BOSS GATE. Three locks. Power at one percent. Be right, not fast, reader.
map.Three locks stand between the crew and V: Three locks stand between the crew and VEX. Lock 1: the engine ring runs 4, 12, 36, 108, __. Lock 2: the power feed needs 5.75 + 3.5. Lock 3: pick the fraction greater than 1/2.
map.Conceptual: three skills, one console —: Conceptual: three skills, one console. Find the multiplying rule. Line up decimal place values. Test each fraction against the 1/2 benchmark.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so multi: Procedural: Lock 1: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so multiply 108 by that same factor. Lock 2: write 3.5 as 3.50, then add by place. Lock 3: half of each denominator is 4.5, 6, and 5. Compare numerators.
map.Systems ONLINE. Hello, crew. I am VEX. A: Systems ONLINE. Hello, crew. I am VEX. Ada Vex left me listening for minds like yours.
map.A question-asker. An evidence-checker. A: One asks questions. One checks proof. One builds. One hunts patterns. And a reader who does the math. I sense problems, but I cannot do math. That part is you.
map.new distortion already. it smells like…: A new problem now. It smells like… bad data. To be continued…
map.Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks t: Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks the next question. This volume: tested the clasp fractions against 1/2.
map.Evidence officer. Charts for every occas: Proof keeper. Charts for each job. This volume: opened the decimal door. Place value kept.
map.Builder and fixer. This volume: unpacked: Builder and fixer. This volume: opened the box one layer at a time. 24 cubic units of hard work.
map.Pattern hunter with a gamer brain. This: Pattern hunter with a gamer brain. This volume: beat the Hall of Sequences with no glitter traps.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine — n: A part of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Now awake. It senses problems. It cannot do math. That's your job.
map.Vexhall's librarian and caretaker. Keepe: Vexhall's book keeper. She keeps Ada's notes. Now she keeps four loud kids too. And one glowing shape.
map.Benchmark.Compare a fraction to a friend: Benchmark.Compare a fraction to an easy number like 1/2. Test the numerator against half the denominator. 3/8 is below 1/2. 5/9 is just above it.
map.Decimals.Line up place values, not end d: Decimals.Line up place values, not the last digits: 3.6 + 2.85 = 6.45 and 12.5 − 4.75 = 7.75.
map.Sequence.An ordered list with a rule — t: Sequence.A list in order with a rule. Test it on every pair. 2, 6, 18, 54 multiplies by 3 → 162. 1, 4, 9, 16 are the squares → 25.
map.Volume.Cubes that fill a box: one layer: Volume.Cubes that fill a box: one layer (4 × 3 = 12) times the layers (× 2) = 24 cubic units.
map.Two-rule pattern.Rules can take turns. W: Two-rule pattern.Rules can take turns. With +5 then ×2, the ring runs 3, 8, 16, 21, 42, 47, 94, 99.
map.\"Patterns are the city's heartbeat. Lea: "Patterns are the city's heartbeat. Learn to count it. Then the city will talk to you." — A.V.
map.completed Volume 1: The Pattern Engine a: finished Volume 1: The Pattern Engine. Can do benchmark fractions. Can do decimal math. Can do number patterns. Can do two-rule sequences. Can do volume.
map.Thank you for waking VEX. Volume 2 is wa: Thank you for waking VEX. Volume 2 waits at the fair gates.
map.A practice clasp offers 2/5 and 4/7, ask: A practice clasp shows 2/5 and 4/7. It wants the one below 1/2.
map.Half of 5 is 2.5 — and 2 < 2.5, so 2/5 s: Half of 5 is 2.5. And 2 < 2.5, so 2/5 is below the benchmark.
map.Half of 7 is 3.5 — and 4 > 3.5, so 4/7 s: Half of 7 is 3.5. And 4 > 3.5, so 4/7 is above. Feed it 2/5.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.What numerator makes ?/8 land exactly ON: What numerator puts ?/8 right ON the 1/2 benchmark?
map.Write 2.4 as 2.40 so the hundredths line: Write 2.4 as 2.40 so the hundredths line up: 2.40 + 1.35.
map.Add by place: 0+5 hundredths, 4+3 tenths: Add by place: 0+5 hundredths, 4+3 tenths, 2+1 ones → 3.75. The dial turns.
map.Test +3: 6 + 3 = 9, but the tile says 12: Test +3: 6 + 3 = 9, but the tile says 12. Adding fails. Test ×2: 3×2=6 ✓, 6×2=12 ✓, 12×2=24 ✓.
map.Rule found: ×2. So the next tile is 24 ×: Rule found: ×2. So the next tile is 24 × 2 = 48.
map.Practice corridor 5, 10, 20, 40 — what's: Practice hall 5, 10, 20, 40. What is the next tile?
A practice box: 5 long, 2 wide, 3 tall.
map.One layer: 5 × 2 = 10 cubes. The box sta: One layer: 5 × 2 = 10 cubes. The box stacks 3 layers high.
map.Volume = 10 × 3 = 30 cubic units. Length: Volume = 10 × 3 = 30 cubic units. Length × width × height. Each time.
map.Volume of a practice box 2 long, 2 wide,: Volume of a practice box 2 long, 2 wide, 5 tall?
map.A practice ring alternates +3, then ×2:: A practice ring uses +3, then ×2. It reads 2, 5, 10, 13, 26.
map.The last move was ×2, so +3 goes next: 2: The last move was ×2, so +3 goes next: 26 + 3 = 29.
map.That practice ring again — what comes af: That test ring again. What comes after 29?
map.Practice console — ring 7, 14, 28: each: Test ring: 7, 14, 28. Each term doubles. So the next is 56.
map.Fraction check 5/8 vs 1/2: half of 8 is: Fraction check 5/8 vs 1/2: half of 8 is 4, and 5 > 4. So 5/8 is above the benchmark.
map.Practice ring once more: what comes afte: Practice ring once more: what comes after 56 (rule ×2)?
map.Both clasps need a choice — tap one butt: Both clasps need a choice. Tap one button in each row.
map.Clasp A stays shut. Test your pick: is i: Clasp A stays shut. Test your pick. Is its numerator under half its denominator? Or over?
map.Clasp B stays shut. 5/9 is only a sliver: Clasp B stays shut. 5/9 is just a bit above 1/2. Check both distances first.
map.3/8 < 1/2 (3 is less than 4), and 5/9 hu: 3/8 < 1/2 (3 is less than 4), and 5/9 is close to the 1/2 benchmark. The clasp opens!
map.6.45 and 7.75 — the dials clack, the bra: 6.45 and 7.75. The dials clack. The brass door rolls aside!
map.A dial sticks. Line up the decimal point: A dial sticks. Line up the decimal points, tenths under tenths. Then work place by place.
map.×3 marches on to 162, and the stars are: ×3 goes on to 162, and the stars are squares: 5 × 5 = 25. The hall lights your path!
map.A number stays dark. Test your rule on E: A number stays dark. Test your rule on EVERY pair of neighbors. Does it work for all of them?
map.12 cubes a layer, 2 layers — 24 cubic un: 12 cubes in a layer. 2 layers. So 24 cubic units. CLICK. The box opens like a flower!
map.The box stays shut. Build it in order: c: The box stays shut. Build it in order: count one 4-by-3 layer first, then stack.
map.47 doubles to 94, then +5 makes 99. The: 47 doubles to 94, then +5 makes 99. The ring spins. The engine door grinds open!
map.The ring jams. Trace the moves: which ru: The ring jams. Trace the moves. Which rule took you INTO 47? Which goes next?
map.Lock 1 holds. The ring multiplies by the: Lock 1 holds. The ring multiplies by the same factor every time. Find it with 12 ÷ 4.
map.Lock 2 holds. Write 3.5 as 3.50, line up: Lock 2 holds. Write 3.5 as 3.50, line up the decimal points, then add.
map.Lock 3 holds. Take half of each denomina: Lock 3 holds. Take half of each denominator. Which numerator is bigger than it?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Gears catch, rings sing,: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Gears catch, rings sing, amber light fills the hall. VEX IS WAKING. Turn the page!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
map.Walk the steps above again — you've got: Walk the steps above again. You can do it.
